newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Przymierze to launch equity fund April 14.
newsitem.headline: Polish Przymierze to launch equity fund April 14.

text.p: The Polish-U.S. mutual fund company Przymierze Towarzystwo Funduszy Powierniczych SA will launch its second fund - aggressive Eurofundusz 2 on April 14, Przymierze's deputy president said on Monday.
Wojciech Gryko told a news conference the company planned to invest about 90 percent of the fund's assets in shares.
He said initially the fund would be investing in 35-45 stocks and the number could increase along with the overall market's growth.
Gryko said the fund would seek high growth stocks set to boost their sales and market share and comparing favourably to other domestic and foreign companies of the same industry.

"We are not going to imitate the WIG index...we will invest on the basis of our own recommendations," he said, adding that Eurofundusz 2 strategy would be shaped by fundamentals and would ignore technical factors.
Przymierze is 51-percent owned by Polish state-owned Bank Pekao SA and 49-percent owned by the U.S.'s Alliance Capital Management LP.
Gryko said the remaining 10 percent of the fund's assets would be invested in bonds, T-bills, commercial papers, bank deposits and foreign securities.

He said the new fund would focus on choosing promising sectors and said that in its currently run balanced Eurofundusz 1 it was overweight in construction, chemicals including pharmaceuticals firms, food sector and insurance.
"Now we are overweight in construction, chemicals such as pharmaceuticals, food industry and insurances as we believe they are prospective sectors," Gryko said.
He said that at the end of last year 40 percent of Eurofundusz 1 were invested in shares, 50 percent were held in bonds and T-bills with the remaining 10 percent held in bank deposits.
